title: A change approved in two clones is not valid until one fresh approval is recorded after the fork
description: A change approved in two clones is not valid until one fresh approval is recorded after the fork
acceptance_criteria: Two clones approve the same change with different actors and each commits. After a merge that keeps one clone's ledger, or both, `change check` and `change audit --strict` refuse, and `change status` reports the approval as not valid, naming both approvers, both commits and the fresh approval.
One `change approve` on the merged branch settles it, and the same commands pass.
Approvals that only append are not a fork, and neither is a change sent back and approved again, or a relay removed or restored by `change repair-relays`.
An archived change whose history holds a fork is not judged again.
Through the binary, the reproduction above is refused, and one fresh approval lets `change check --commit` pass.

answers.constraints: Leif's 2026-11-13 recovery choice, one fresh approval; #428's rule stays as approved: this walk adds the other side of each merge, for definition approvals only; the change lesson that a printed recovery command must work as printed.
